_step_title: Press operations — correct fixture / driver selection
_recorded_by: Comer process engineering (top line errors), relayed by Omnia 2026-06-11

facts.fact: Incorrect fixture/driver selection at the press station is one of the TWO most frequent line errors on this build (the other is the step-6 bearing-cone orientation). Step 1's cup press uses PUNCH FIXTURE cod.3187.111.100.09 — verify the engraved code on the fixture before pressing.

citation.transcript_quote: Incorrect Fixture and Driver Selection: this is particularly an issue at the press station.

facts.fact: Wrong fixture/driver picks happen almost exclusively during cross-training or shift coverage: regular operators know the tooling by memory, but a cross-trained backup covering for an operator on leave is much more likely to select the wrong driver. The correct drivers and fixtures are detailed in the Work Instructions — when in doubt, read the engraved cod. number off the tool and check it against the step.
facts.applies_when: cross-trained backup or shift-coverage operator is running the station

citation.transcript_quote: If a regular operator is on leave, a cross-trained backup is much more likely to select the wrong driver.

facts.fact: The press tooling is easy to confuse because most of it shares the 3187.111.* family and differs only in the last digits of the engraved code: step 1 punch fixture cod.3187.111.100.09, step 4 punch cod.3187.111.100.07, step 6 driver cod.3187.111.180.00, step 8 punch fixture cod.3187.111.100.27, step 14 driver cod.3187.111.100.28. The engraved code is the reliable check — do not pick by eye, especially between the 100.07 and the 100.09.
